Defer CloudProfileReportingService scheduler creation to BEST_EFFORT

Unconditionally observing CloudPolicyCore in Init() caused
OnCoreConnected() to run synchronously during startup before
BEST_EFFORT UI tasks are enabled, moving UploadReportOnProfileOpen
uploads into the initial DMServer startup burst alongside policy
fetches.

Keep CloudPolicyCore observation active across account switches, but
schedule scheduler creation on BEST_EFFORT from both Init() and
OnCoreConnected() while still tearing down stale mismatched clients
synchronously on reconnect.

actor: Convert AttemptLogin to use a custom dispatcher

Convert AttemptLoginTool into the first "composite tool". The
ToolRequest creates a dispatcher which first dispatches an internal
version of the AttemptLoginToolRequest which invokes the
AttemptLoginTool. If that succeeds the dispatcher sends a
ClickToolRequest.

This sequence was previously achieved with EnqueueFollowup which is now
removed.

The result-merging helpers are moved from execution_engine.cc into
tool_result.{h,cc} so they can be shared. The end state should be that
ExecutionEngine doesn't need to merge results, only composite tools.

[selection] Track frame token with context menu text selections

Context menu text invocations updated GlicSelectionObserver's selected
text without recording the source frame token, causing subsequent
selection overlay invocations to fail to resolve selection bounds even
while the side panel displayed the shared text. Merge both context menu
update helpers into UpdateSelectionStateFromContextMenu() requiring the
target RenderFrameHost so text and frame token are updated together.

[PM] Add option for FrameAudibleVoter to vote USER_VISIBLE

Adds the "audible_frame_user_visible_priority" param (default false) to
kPMProcessPriorityPolicy. When true, audible frames vote for
base::Process::Priority::kUserVisible instead of kUserBlocking.

With UserVisibleProcessPriority disabled (default), kUserVisible is
remapped to kUserBlocking at the OS level in
RenderProcessHostImpl::UpdateProcessPriority(), so this only affects
renderer-side consumers of the process priority (isolate priority with
IsolatesPriorityUseProcessPriority, RestrictThreadPoolInBackground).
The audio rendering thread is realtime regardless of process priority.

This lets hidden audible renderers keep v8's memory-saving GC behaviour
(e.g. combined with IsolatesPriorityUserVisibleAsBestEffort) without
lowering their OS priority.

[iOS] Fix Stay Safe and Made for iOS buckets in promo Shown histogram

`IOS.DefaultBrowserPromo.Shown` was recorded by casting
`DefaultPromoType` to `DefaultPromoTypeForUMA`, but the two enums order
Stay Safe and Made for iOS differently. Stay Safe impressions were
logged as Made for iOS and vice versa, so past data for these two
buckets is swapped.

- Map the promo type to its UMA bucket explicitly.
- Note the swapped buckets in the histogram summary.

[Multiprofile] Add PreNativeProfileKeyedMap

Some objects are created before native is initialized, when there is no
Profile yet, but belong to a profile. With multiple profiles, such an
object must end up with the profile it was set up for.

PreNativeProfileKeyedMap wraps ProfileKeyedMap.
1. The map takes the factory in its constructor, like the destroy
   action. Before native is initialized, getForProfile(null) returns a
   single pre-native instance, created by the factory with a null
   profile, for the profile Chrome is expected to start with, whose base
   name (ProfileManager.getLastUsedProfileBaseName()) is read when the
   pre-native instance is created.
2. The pre-native instance is moved to that profile when the profile, or
   one of its off-the-record profiles, is first requested, or when it is
   the first regular profile added. Profiles are matched by comparing
   Profile.getBaseName() of the original profile with the recorded base
   name.
3. If the first regular profile added is another one, or no base name
   was recorded, the pre-native instance is destroyed, and the profile
   gets a new object when it is requested.
4. Once the first profile is added, callers must pass a profile. Objects
   are destroyed with their profile, as in ProfileKeyedMap, or when the
   map is destroyed.

Follow-up CLs will use the map for objects that are created before
native.

Test: chrome_junit_tests -f '*PreNativeProfileKeyedMapTest*'

[css] Snapshot cross-fade clients before notifying ImageChanged

When a cross-fade's underlying image fails (e.g. via window.stop()),
CSSCrossfadeValue::ObserverProxy forwards ImageChanged to every client.
A client <img> using the cross-fade as generated content then switches
to fallback content, which creates its UA shadow root and synchronously
detaches its children's layout objects. Those children are themselves
clients of the same cross-fade, so CSSImageGeneratorValue::clients_ is
modified while being iterated.

Iterate over a snapshot of the clients instead, and skip clients that
were removed during dispatch.

Key NthIndexCache on QualifiedName instead of tagName()

NthIndexCache keyed :nth-of-type() and :nth-last-of-type() entries by
Element::tagName(), which omits the element's namespace URI and
uppercases HTML tag names. Elements in different namespaces with the
same serialized tagName() (such as an HTML div and a foreign DIV, or
elements with the same local name in two foreign namespaces) collided on
the same cache entry and reused each other's sibling count in
NthLastOfTypeIndex().

Key NthIndexCache::Key on QualifiedName using local name and namespace
URI matching (matching QualifiedName::Matches()), and add DCHECKs in
NthOfTypeIndex() and NthLastOfTypeIndex() against the uncached counts.

parent
99aa4e6c25f1f88e923822c5f7f0556911a164b6 [ diff ] 
[TabModel] Run resumeSaveTabList callbacks when the save is cancelled

Moving a tab group to another window pauses tab list saving, detaches
the tabs, and then calls TabPersistentStore#resumeSaveTabList() with a
callback that launches the target window. The callback waited for the
pending tab list save to finish. If that save was cancelled first, the
callback never ran, so the detached tabs were never handed to the target
window. The save is cancelled when the store is destroyed, for example
because the source window closed once it became empty, and when
saveState() replaces it with a synchronous save as the window stops.

Keep the pending callbacks in the store. On destroy(), let an in-flight
SaveListTask finish writing its already-extracted metadata and run the
callbacks from onPostExecute() (skipping observer notifications after
teardown), so moved tabs are removed from the source metadata file
before callbacks attach them elsewhere; calls to resumeSaveTabList()
after destroy() still wait on an in-flight SaveListTask if one exists
and post directly otherwise. In saveState(), run the callbacks after the
StrictMode finally block once the synchronous metadata and tab state
writes complete.

[Android] Fix AreaMotionEventFilter hover-exit MotionEvent use-after-recycle

AreaMotionEventFilter.onHoverEventInternal() allocated a synthetic
ACTION_HOVER_EXIT MotionEvent via MotionEvent.obtain(e) and immediately
called recycle() on it before reading getActionMasked() and dispatching
it.

Handle mHoverExitedArea directly on the incoming MotionEvent without
allocating or recycling a synthetic event.

[Autofill] Inherit is_embedded from parent in Create[AndActivate]AutofillDriver()

Before this CL, callers of Create[AndActivate]AutofillDriver() with a
non-null `parent` had to pass `is_embedded` explicitly if `parent` was
embedded.

This CL changes `CreateAutofillDriverParams::is_embedded` to
`std::optional<bool>`, defaulting to `parent->IsEmbedded()` when
`parent` is non-null (and `false` otherwise). Any explicit mismatch is
caught by `TestAutofillDriverFactory::CheckValidFrameTree()`.

Reland "Make AppliedTextDecoration equality independent of :visited"

This is a reland of commit 5cf568039baef934b5d67d4d0bbc34b15e240934.

crrev.com/c/8734802 landed after CQ+1 and added a per-element DOMNodeId
source_id to PrecomputedHoverState, causing the test equality check
between two distinct <a> elements to fail. Update the test to compare
PrecomputedHoverState presence, is_current_visible, and IsInEffect().

Original change's description:
> Make AppliedTextDecoration equality independent of :visited
>
> TextDecorationOf() stored the color picked by VisitedDependentColor()
> in AppliedTextDecoration, and operator== compared it. Visited and
> unvisited links therefore produced different style diffs and
> different decoration run merging, which is observable and leaks
> history. Store both the unvisited and visited colors plus a bit
> saying which one to paint, and compare only the two colors.
> PrecomputedHoverChangesTextDecoration() had the same dependency and
> now compares both colors as well.
>
> Fixed: 578663704

Drop intents received during startup

If we receive an intent during startup we get an inconsistent view of
what surface or webpage we're launching into since startup is async.

Drop any intents sent during startup - any intents received this way are
most likely either malicious or programmatic bugs (apps that double-fire
intents).

viz/mac: Share an os_workgroup with the threads of the display pipeline

Create a shared "CrDisplayFrame" os_workgroup_interval in
FrameSinkManagerImpl on Apple Silicon so that threads in the display
pipeline run in the same XNU thread group.

When base::mac::kMacWorkgroupInterval is enabled, VizCompositorThread
creates the workgroup, configures the GPU process foreground workgroup
at ThreadType::kPresentation (covering CrGpuMain, CompositorGpuThread,
GPU IO, and presentation workers), and passes a Mach send right to
clients via CompositorFrameSink::RequestWorkgroupPort().
AsyncLayerTreeFrameSink joins CrBrowserMain for UI sinks and configures
the process foreground workgroup in renderers, which RenderThreadImpl
toggles in OnRendererHidden() and OnRendererVisible().

No intervals are reported on the workgroup here. A follow-up reports
display frames as intervals behind a separate feature.

Design doc:
https://docs.google.com/document/d/1REbY_wVI81slFqdfcGGxHTzimZxJg4AIkrYtx21gxOw/edit

Test: viz_unittests --gtest_filter="*MacWorkgroup*"

[iOS] Skip no-op pref updates in PromosManagerImpl

Opening a ScopedListPrefUpdate or ScopedDictPrefUpdate always reports
the pref as changed, which notifies observers and schedules a write of
the Preferences file, even when the value does not change.

PromosManagerImpl did this on hot paths:
- WhatsNewSceneAgent re-registers its promo on every foreground of
  every scene, and registering an already-registered promo erased and
  re-appended it.
- Deregistering opened updates on all three promo prefs, even when the
  promo was in none of them. The default browser scene agent issues a
  burst of such deregistrations at startup.

Only open an update when the pref will actually change. Active promo
lists are read into a std::set, so not moving a re-registered promo to
the end of its list has no behavior impact.

[downloads] Add UMA metrics for the Android download toolbar button

Adds four histograms to measure download toolbar button usage and tray
diagnostics on Android desktop:

- Android.DownloadToolbarButton.Clicked: records the button's visual
  state (InProgress, CompleteActive, CompleteInactive) when clicked.
- Android.DownloadToolbarButton.Shown: records once per show cycle per
  window without double-counting across incognito/regular tab switches.
- Android.DownloadTray.FullTray.RowCount: records the row count (0-30)
  when opening the full tray (0 on fallback to full download history).
- Android.DownloadTray.CompletionPopup.NotShownReason: records why a due
  completion popup was not shown (AlreadyShowing, WindowUnfocused,
  TooSoon, WindowNotVisible, AnchorHidden, NothingNew, or ShowFailed).

Restore gating for adding AccessibilityNodeInfo.MathInfo

This CL restores the AccessibilityAndroidMath feature flag gating
for adding AccessibilityNodeInfo.MathInfo

With this CL, AccessibilityNodeInfo.MathInfo is added whenever
the AccessibilityAndroidMath feature flag is on but
irrespective of the Android Talkback version.

The rationale is to enable disabling the feature using
solely the Chrome feature. This avoids having to synchronize
disabling the feature via Chrome variations and via Talkback
server flags. The AccessibilityNodeInfo.MathInfo code is not
gated on the Talkback version in order to increase
confidence that the AccessibilityAndroidMath feature won't
cause any regressions.

When the feature is enabled in Talkback, but disabled in
Chrome the current code leaves the user in a broken state.

[Linux/X11] Don't advertise maximize for non-maximizable windows

X11Window only set the decorations field of _MOTIF_WM_HINTS, so window
managers assumed every window could be maximized. On Cinnamon, dragging
a Picture-in-Picture window to a screen edge made Muffin edge-tile it
to half the screen (_NET_WM_STATE_MAXIMIZED_VERT).

When the delegate's CanMaximize() is false, also set the functions
field of _MOTIF_WM_HINTS, listing every function except maximize.
Muffin then drops the maximize action and no longer tiles the window.
The hints are updated again when the size constraints change.

Restrict session restore targets to normal tabbed browser windows

AndroidLiveTabContext::FindContextWithID previously selected any
non-incognito TabModel for the profile (including non-tabbed, headless,
or unassociated models with an invalid SessionID), and
FindContextForWebContents did not validate the window SessionID or
TabModel type. Similarly, FindBrowserWindowInterfaceWithProfile in
sessions_api.cc matched non-normal browser windows.

Filter AndroidLiveTabContext lookups to standard, tabbed, non-incognito
TabModels matching the profile with a valid window SessionID, and filter
FindBrowserWindowInterfaceWithProfile to TYPE_NORMAL windows so tab
restoration only targets regular tabbed browser windows.

[ozone/wayland] Keep active bubble across toplevel deactivation

When a toplevel lost OS activation, WaylandToplevelWindow cleared
`active_bubble_`, so on reactivation the toplevel itself was activated
instead of the bubble that was active before. For an extension action
popup, activating the browser widget tree closes the popup, so opening
a native file chooser from the popup (or switching to another app and
back) closed it.

Keep `active_bubble_` when the toplevel is deactivated, still notifying
the bubble that it lost activation, and notify the bubble rather than
the toplevel when the toplevel is reactivated. crrev.com/c/8869407 does
the same for child widgets in DesktopNativeWidgetAura, which covers
X11.

77ad57957e8497f329a3bd78d80778fa1aa3ef12
parent
cdb2ce7ab2bad14770380be2253c0aee00da7bb8 [ diff ] 
[X11] Use per-monitor work areas from _GTK_WORKAREAS_D<n>

_NET_WORKAREA is a single rectangle for the whole screen, so on
multi-monitor setups Chrome applied it to at most one display, and
panels on other monitors (or on an edge shared between monitors) were
ignored. window.screen.avail* then reported the full monitor bounds.

Mutter-based window managers (GNOME Shell, Cinnamon's Muffin) also set
_GTK_WORKAREAS_D<desktop>, a list of per-monitor work areas, and
advertise it with _GTK_WORKAREAS in _NET_SUPPORTED. When available,
intersect each display's bounds with those rectangles, as GTK does in
gdk_x11_monitor_get_workarea(), and fall back to _NET_WORKAREA
otherwise. ConvertDisplayBoundsToDips() now keeps work area insets,
and the display list is refreshed when the property or the current
desktop changes.

[PM] Replace FrameNode::IsIntersectingLargeArea with 3-state enum

FrameNode::IsIntersectingLargeArea() was a boolean defaulting to true to
encode ImportantFrameDecorator's "unknown -> important" fallback policy
directly in the graph node. Its value was overridden when the viewport
intersection was kNotIntersecting, making the exact relationship between
various ViewportIntersection states and the "intersecting large area"
concept hard to reason about.

Replace IsIntersectingLargeArea(), SetIsIntersectingLargeArea(), and
OnIsIntersectingLargeAreaChanged() with ViewportIntersectionArea
({kUnknown, kSmallOrNone, kLarge}) via GetViewportIntersectionArea() and
OnViewportIntersectionAreaChanged():

- Outermost main frames return kLarge unless overridden. (Because they
  are assumed to intersect the entire viewport.
  `is_intersecting_large_area_` was not updated for these frames so
  stayed at the default true.)

- Clamped to kUnknown while GetViewportIntersection() is kUnknown, and
  to kSmallOrNone while not kIntersecting.
  (`is_intersecting_large_area_` used the default true for kUnknown, and
  clamped to false when not kIntersecting.)

- Same-process child frames inherit their parent's area before
  OnViewportIntersectionChanged() fires so observers never see torn
  state, while ImportantFrameDecorator explicitly handles kUnknown ->
  true.

Also replaces SetIsIntersectingLargeAreaImpl() with
SetViewportIntersectionAndArea(), which is called whenever either the
ViewportIntersection or ViewportIntersectionArea changes. This ensures
the correct observers are notified whenever the caller-visible result of
GetViewportIntersection() or GetViewportIntersectionArea() changes.

Factors out checks used when updating ViewportIntersection to helper
functions to ensure ViewportIntersection and ViewportIntersectionArea
are treated consistently.

Test: components_browsertests (*PerformanceManager*)
Test: browser_tests (*FrameNodeImplBrowserTest*)

[partition_alloc] Enable user space zero segment on ASan builds

Previously, `enable_user_space_zero_segment` required
`use_partition_alloc_as_malloc`, leaving the first 4 GiB + 1 MiB
unprotected on ASan builds. On 64-bit Linux x64 ASan, `LowMem`
is unmapped and `LowShadow` is mapped `PROT_READ | PROT_WRITE`, so
uninstrumented V8 JIT/Wasm accesses to low addresses can write into
`LowShadow` instead of faulting and trigger false-positive V8 sandbox
violation reports.

This CL enables the user space zero segment on 64-bit Linux, ChromeOS,
and Android ASan builds:
It achieves this by running `InitZeroSegmentForAsan()` via a priority-101
constructor when `!USE_PARTITION_ALLOC_AS_MALLOC` which runs immediately
after ASan's `.preinit_array` setup.
The constructor reserves `LowMem` as `PROT_NONE` before modifying
`LowShadow` to PROT_READ, and bailing out gracefully if pre-existing
low mappings (e.g., non-PIE binaries or non-Native-Zygote Android
ART) or `ASAN_OPTIONS=protect_shadow_gap=0` are present.

SettingsPageFragmentDelegateImpl registered fresh
this::updateBackPressState method references on the host and
multi-column child FragmentManagers without keeping references to
remove them in destroySettings(). Store a single

multi-column child FragmentManagers, register via
getHostFragmentManager() and getChildFragmentManagerOrNull(), and
unregister the listener in destroySettings().

[iOS] Add options field to RemoteActorPasswordUploadRequest proto

This change extends the existing RemoteActorPasswordUploadRequest proto
with the following behaviors:

1. Callers can specify `options` to indicate whether they want to use
   an existing saved credential or add a new one
2. Operation-specific data (e.g., the details of the cred to add) are
   included in new structs

This is backwards- and forwards-compatible:
* Calls including the new fields sent to old Chromium clients will
  proceed as if the new fields didn't exist
* Calls from old remote actor clients that don't explicitly set a
  value for `options` will fall back to the existing behavior

[Default Browser] Move setter result handling into the manager

Prefactor for having DefaultBrowserManager own running setters.

DefaultBrowserController recorded Result, OutcomeV2 and SuccessDuration
when its setter finished, then showed the success toast or asked the
manager to start the failure tracker and survey. That now lives in
DefaultBrowserManager::HandleSetterResult(), which the controller calls.
The controller still owns and runs the setter.

Behavior change: if a setter finishes after the manager is gone (after
the main loop stops at shutdown), its result is no longer recorded.
Before, Result and OutcomeV2 were still recorded in that case.

[PA] Prefetch slots ahead of their release in SLQ full purges

A full purge of a SchedulerLoopQuarantineBranch (e.g. at the end of a
task) releases all quarantined slots. Releasing a slot writes to its
first bytes: ThreadCache::PutInBucket() writes a freelist entry [1] and
BatchFreeQueue::Purge() writes a zero before it acquires the partition
lock [2]. After a task that quarantined many slots, these slots may no
longer be in the CPU cache.

This CL makes a full purge prefetch the slot that it releases 16
iterations later. Other purges are unchanged: they stop as soon as the
branch is below its target size, so they do not necessarily release the
prefetched slot.

SchedulerLoopQuarantinePerfTest results on Pinpoint for the browser
main thread configuration ("all lines" rows read every cache line of
each object before freeing it, like a destructor that reads all
fields):

Significance: ◆ p < 0.05, ◆◆ p < 0.01, ◆◆◆ p < 0.001

Android: Fix washed-out dark mode colors for synced themes

Theme colors synced from another device looked noticeably paler in dark
mode than the same color picked locally, and pure black (#000000) seed
colors produced a pink accent instead of blue. Synced colors now match
the built-in color choices and desktop Chrome, and the pure-black seed
fix now applies to all dynamic palette callers in `ui/color`. Unapplied
synced colors update on restart or when the synced theme changes; an
already-applied synced custom color updates when re-selected from the
synced device's swatch.

[PerformanceManager] Merge PageLoadTrackerDecoratorHelper into PageLoadTrackerDecorator

Now that PerformanceManager runs on the UI thread, the separate
PageLoadTrackerDecoratorHelper class is no longer needed.

Move the per-WebContents WebContentsObserver into
PageLoadTrackerDecorator as NodeAttachedDataImpl<WebContentsObserver>,
created in OnPageNodeAdded() and cleaned up automatically with
PageNodeImpl. This eliminates PageLoadTrackerDecoratorHelper, its
intrusive linked list, the public static
DidStartLoading/PrimaryPageChanged/DidStopLoading entry points, and its
separate wiring in ChromeBrowserMainExtraPartsPerformanceManager.

[TabPersistentStore] Save cancelled in-flight tab in saveState

When TabPersistentStore starts saving a tab asynchronously, it snapshots
the tab's state and marks the tab as clean on the UI thread before the
background disk write actually runs. If a synchronous saveState() (for
example, on backgrounding or teardown) happens while that write is still
queued or in flight, two issues occur:

1. Cancelling a queued task re-checked the tab's dirtiness state, saw it
   was already marked clean, and skipped saving the tab to disk, losing
   its persisted state.
2. Cancelling a task that had already started writing did not wait for
   the background write to finish before saveState() returned.

Ensure that saveState() either cancels the pending write before it
begins or waits for an in-progress write to finish. If the tab was not
written to disk, re-queue it unconditionally (as long as it is not
destroyed) so it is saved synchronously, and ignore completion callbacks
from tasks that have already been superseded.

Reland "[Dictation] Move WebContents and key observation into DomTarget"

This is a reland of commit c3f174bbe519a9079237be17d2d3fdb59870e2b5

Changes since original CL:

Fix a pre-existing freed-pointer comparison in
AutoSessionEndDelayedShutdownCancelledByNewStream (in
DictationSessionControllerTest). The test saved a raw pointer to the
first StreamProvider, waited for PurgeToDeleteStreamProviders() to
destroy it via WaitForPostedTasks(), started a second stream, and then
asserted EXPECT_NE(stream_provider1, stream_provider2), which failed
when the allocator reused the freed slot (observed deterministically on
linux-chromeos-dbg after MockStreamProvider's size changed). Assert that
attached_stream_provider() is null after the first stream finishes
instead of comparing the freed pointer.

Original change's description:
> [Dictation] Move WebContents and key observation into DomTarget
>
> Move WebContentsObserver and RenderWidgetHostObserver (Escape, Enter,
> typing, focus change, navigation, crash, and WebContents destruction)
> from SessionController into DomTarget behind a new Target::Delegate
> interface (SetDelegate() and SetStreamActive()).
>
> Transfer ownership of Target from StreamProvider to SessionController
> via StreamEntry and idle_target_, and update
> StreamProvider::BindToTargetAndConnect() to borrow Target& with an
> explicit DetachTarget() cleanup hook before asynchronous provider
> deletion.
>
> This decouples SessionController from DOM/WebContents internals so
> non-DOM targets do not observe unrelated page input or lifecycle events,
> with no behavior change for DOM dictation sessions.
>

[iOS, Duo] Add VerticalSidebarViewController

While iPhone Duo is folded, the toolbar's control buttons will move to
a vertical sidebar over the system vertical bar column. This CL adds
its view controller, which doesn't depend on the IA:
- It shows back and forward on top, then new tab and tab grid, and the
  tools menu at the bottom, in a VerticalSidebarView. The buttons come
  from ToolbarButtonFactory, and are shown whatever the size class.
- It's a ToolbarButtonsConsumer, so ToolbarButtonsMediator gives it the
  buttons' state and menus, and ToolbarButtonActions handles its taps.
  As in the toolbar, taps on its navigation buttons disabled while an
  actor controls the tab show the actor's interaction-limited snackbar.
- While active, its buttons own the named layout guides of the
  toolbar's buttons. It releases them when it becomes inactive.
- It shows the tools menu IPH highlight and blue dot.

It isn't used yet.

[Android] Fix overlay panel size change and observer leak

Fix two bugs in OverlayPanelAnimation and OverlayPanelBase:
- OverlayPanelAnimation.handleSizeChanged() used an inverted null check
  (mAnimatingState == null || mAnimatingState != UNDEFINED), animating
  panel height to 0 on idle size changes instead of resizing.
  cancelHeightAnimation() also left mAnimatingState set, allowing a
  subsequent handleSizeChanged() to restart a canceled animation.
- OverlayPanelBase registered an anonymous
  BrowserControlsStateProvider.Observer that was never removed in
  destroy().

Make mAnimatingState a primitive @PanelState int initialized to
PanelState.UNDEFINED, fix the handleSizeChanged() check, reset
mAnimatingState/mAnimatingStateReason in cancelHeightAnimation(),
unregister the browser controls observer in destroy(), and add focused
regression tests in OverlayPanelBaseTest.

Fix Windows hang in DoubleNestedRunLoop tab drag test

After the Kombucha migration, the mouse release was sent in a separate
step after the one that calls TabDragController::Drag() twice. On
Windows the drag then never ended and the test timed out waiting for
kTabDragActiveState.

Send the release from inside the same step that calls Drag(), as the
test did before the migration, then wait for the drag to end.

Verified on Win11 Swarming: 60/60 timeouts before, 100/100 passes after.
Also passes locally on Linux X11 and ChromeOS.

Show menu mnemonics when a menu is opened from the keyboard

Context menus opened with Shift+F10 or the Menu key did not underline
mnemonics on Linux (or ChromeOS) unless Alt was held when the menu
opened. MenuRunnerImpl::ShouldShowMnemonics() only checked
SHOULD_SHOW_MNEMONICS and the Alt modifier and ignored the menu source
type, so keyboard-invoked context menus, which pass
MenuSourceType::kKeyboard, showed no underlines even though the
mnemonics worked.

Show mnemonics whenever the menu source type is kKeyboard (including
INVOKED_FROM_KEYBOARD menus with no explicit source). Menus opened with
the mouse are unchanged, and macOS still never shows mnemonics.

Open the edit profile dialog from the Mac and Linux menu bars

When kReplaceManageProfileWithDialog is enabled, "Edit…" in the Mac
menu bar Profiles menu and in the Linux global menu bar opens the
profile customization dialog in the edit profile mode instead of
chrome://settings/manageProfile.

Both go through AvatarMenu::EditProfile(), which only has a profile. The
new chrome::ShowManageProfileForProfile() activates a browser of the
profile, or opens one, and shows the dialog on top of it.

Demo: crbug.com/585482119#comment4

[iOS][Intelligence] Restrict Gemini Actor to non-Duo iPhones

Returns false from `IsGeminiActorEnabled()` on tablet (`iPad`) and
`iPhone Duo` (`IsDuoDevice()`) form factors so user-facing Gemini Actor
and backgrounding entrypoints remain restricted to standard iPhones.

Adds unit tests covering both non-Duo iPhone enablement and tablet/Duo
exclusion, and guards existing `IsGeminiActorEnabled()`-dependent tests
on unsupported form factors.

[iOS] Remove the unused full worklog from the worklog view controller.

The full worklog has been hidden in the worklog view controller since
the worklog moved inline in Gemini responses, where taps on suggestion
cards are now handled by the inline worklog provider. This removes the
hidden copy and its scroll view, so the view controller only shows the
header and, in compact mode, the current step.

The worklog view itself is unchanged, as the inline worklog still uses
it. Tests now check the compact worklog instead of the full one.

[iOS] Lay out the actuation sheet as header, content and footer.

During a task, the worklog is pinned to the top of the Gemini container
and the intervention to the bottom. At the large detent, the worklog
shrinks to its header and the conversation fills the space in between,
keeping the intervention visible. The full timeline and its egtest are
removed, as Gemini responses show it inline.

The container now owns the worklog's visibility and measures both
pieces, re-measuring the intervention when the sheet's width changes.
The header no longer insets from the safe area, so it keeps its height
under the status bar.

Swiping towards the minimized detent now slides the intervention out at
the bottom instead of over the worklog.

[iOS] Move the actuation intervention into its own view controller.

Moves the intervention out of the actuation worklog view controller into
a new view controller with its own consumer and mutator, driven by the
same mediator. The Gemini container lays it out at the bottom, below the
worklog, and includes it in the medium detent height, keeping the
current appearance. This lets the container place the intervention
independently of the worklog in a follow-up.

[iOS] Show the running task's worklog live in Gemini responses.

The inline worklog of the response running an agent task now follows the
task's data source instead of its block. The view stays empty until the
data source arrives, then expands, applies updates incrementally with
ComputeActuationWorklogEntriesDiff, and keeps its final live content
once the task ends. Views of other responses keep showing their block.

During actuation, the large detent now shows the Gemini conversation
instead of the full worklog, so the live inline worklog is visible
without being shown twice. The minimized and medium detents are
unchanged. The full worklog becomes unreachable and will be removed in a
follow-up. Until the inline worklog handles suggestion taps, suggestion
cards can only be tapped from the compact worklog.

[Android] Fix OverlayPanelEventFilter MotionEvent leaks and stale replay

OverlayPanelEventFilter leaked obtained MotionEvents when clearing
mRecordedEvents and in propagateEvent(), and reset() left stale recorded
events (plus mFilterHadDownEvent) that replayed on subsequent gestures.

Recycle all recorded MotionEvents in clearRecordedEvents()/reset(), drop
the redundant mIsRecordingEvents flag in favor of checking
!mRecordedEvents.isEmpty(), recycle the synthetic down MotionEvent in
propagateEvent(), and add a regression test in
OverlayPanelEventFilterTest.

Add container overloads to MakeFixedFlatMap/Set

Add overloads to base::MakeFixedFlatMap and base::MakeFixedFlatSet that
accept fixed-size containers (std::array, base::fixed_flat_map, and
base::fixed_flat_set) with optional comparator and projection arguments,
matching base::MakeFlatMap and base::MakeFlatSet's
(range, comp = {}, proj = {}) parameter order and explicit key/mapped
type convention.

This avoids raw C-array boilerplate when constructing compile-time
lookup tables from std::array or deriving one fixed_flat_map or
fixed_flat_set from another (such as inverting a map or extracting its
keys).

Also update the existing C-array overload of base::MakeFixedFlatSet to
skip sorting when the input is already sorted and unique, matching
base::MakeFixedFlatMap.

[perf] Disable PersistentCachePerftest.Create on Windows

PersistentCachePerftest.Create/{JournalModeWal,MultipleConnections,
MultipleConnectionsWal,SingleConnection} hit the 45s test launcher
timeout on every win-10-perf run, so components_perftests fails at the
benchmark level in every build (323 failed / 0 passed over the last 30
days in LUCI Analysis). This keeps win-10-perf red. Disable the Create
case on Windows, following the Android disables already tracked in this
bug.

Revert "[Dictation] Move WebContents and key observation into DomTarget"

This reverts commit c3f174bbe519a9079237be17d2d3fdb59870e2b5.

Reason for revert:
DictationSessionControllerTest.AutoSessionEndDelayedShutdownCancelledByNewStream
is failing in unit_tests on linux-chromeos-dbg (build #47527):

chrome/browser/dictation/session_controller_unittest.cc:1212: Failure
Expected: (stream_provider1) != (stream_provider2), actual: 0x5c870b574500 vs 0x5c870b574500

Original change's description:
> [Dictation] Move WebContents and key observation into DomTarget
>
> Move WebContentsObserver and RenderWidgetHostObserver (Escape, Enter,
> typing, focus change, navigation, crash, and WebContents destruction)
> from SessionController into DomTarget behind a new Target::Delegate
> interface (SetDelegate() and SetStreamActive()).
>
> Transfer ownership of Target from StreamProvider to SessionController
> via StreamEntry and idle_target_, and update
> StreamProvider::BindToTargetAndConnect() to borrow Target& with an
> explicit DetachTarget() cleanup hook before asynchronous provider
> deletion.
>
> This decouples SessionController from DOM/WebContents internals so
> non-DOM targets do not observe unrelated page input or lifecycle events,
> with no behavior change for DOM dictation sessions.
>

GPU results for erf, pow and l2Pool2d on Intel Mac and got the last two
Dawn rolls reverted. Let these tests either pass or fail on Mac14 and
Mac15 so Chromium stays green with or without that Dawn change. Once
the roll sticks, the baselines can be updated and the suppressions
removed.

[SuperSize] Preserve relative archive paths for 32/64-bit disassembly

The Android binary size reference generator stages both 32-bit and
64-bit size configs into the same directory. Since switching from
Trichrome to standalone Chrome/WebView, both configs archive an
unstripped libchrome.so under different subdirectories, so flattening
paths to basenames caused the 64-bit libchrome.so to overwrite the
32-bit one and produce wrong "before" disassembly on 32-bit diffs.

Also verify ELF build IDs before disassembling so mismatched binaries
(such as flat reference zips during rollout) are skipped cleanly.

[Android] Cancel stale BitmapFetcher in ContextualSearchSceneLayer

ContextualSearchSceneLayer::FetchThumbnail() returned early on an empty
URL without resetting fetcher_, and HideTree() did not cancel in-flight
fetches or clear thumbnail_url_, allowing stale thumbnails to apply
after clearing or hiding the panel.

Reset fetcher_ at the start of FetchThumbnail() and reset fetcher_ /
clear thumbnail_url_ in HideTree().

[Public Transit] Use WebPageFacility in fullscreen/context menu tests

Migrate FullscreenVideoTest and ContextMenuDragTest from DOMUtils to
WebPageFacility and HtmlElement:
- FullscreenVideoTest: click #fullscreen in a Trip that waits for the
  new TabFullscreenCondition and a non-null fullscreen video size. This
  uses the default Trip timeout (5 s) instead of the old sequential
  6 s + 3 s waits, and reads getFullscreenVideoSize() on the UI thread.
  Media play/pause calls are out of scope for this bug.
- ContextMenuDragTest: read the image bounds from HtmlElement#value()
  instead of DOMUtils#getNodeBounds(). The bounds are taken when the
  page loads and only anchor the relative drag deltas the test checks.

TabFullscreenCondition reuses FullscreenTestUtils' fullscreen flag and
window insets checks, now public, and reports which one is not
fulfilled yet. isFullscreenFlagSet() drops its unused Activity
parameter. Timeouts now throw TravelException instead of
CriteriaHelper.TimeoutException or TimeoutException.

Skip receiving Mach vouchers in the browser process

Per-message Mach voucher deallocation in ipcz_driver::Envelope::Close()
contributes to Browser Main and IO thread congestion on macOS, even
though the browser process already runs at foreground priority and does
not benefit from XNU task importance donation from child processes.

It's possible that some Mojo receivers in the browser process are bound
to lower-priority threads, but they currently don't need vouchers either
since Chrome doesn't apply the voucher to the receiving thread (eg. with
thread_set_mach_voucher). Holding an unadopted voucher only donates
process-level importance and doesn't boost the QoS of lower-priority
threads within the process.

Add enable_mach_vouchers (default true) to mojo::core::Configuration and
a kSkipMachVouchersInBrowser feature checked in content/app so that only
the Chrome browser process disables vouchers. Standalone Mojo brokers
(such as macOS PWA app shims and updater daemons) continue receiving
vouchers.

Also fixes an IWYU error (misspelled include) and removes the static
`enabled` variable in ShouldUseVouchers(): it has lower importance now
that FeatureList has an internal cache, and this prevents the state from
being incorrectly cached across tests that re-initialize features.

android_app_bundle, and create_size_info_files so packaging actions

[Dino Delight] Add Dino bookmark IPH trigger and eligibility controller

Adds `dino::CanShowDinoBookmarkPrompt()` and
`dino::MaybeTriggerDinoBookmarkPrompt()` to `chrome/browser/dino/` to
centralize eligibility checks and promo triggering for the offline Dino
game-over bookmark IPH (Windows, Mac, Linux).

Eligibility guards:
- `dino::kDinoDelight` master feature flag enabled
- `PromotionsEnabled` enterprise policy enabled (checked explicitly
  because `FeaturePromoController` does not enforce it on Toast IPHs)
- Visible offline error page (excluding `chrome://dino/`)
- Non-OTR profile with `kEditBookmarksEnabled`
- `kDinoBookmarkPromptMaxTimesShownCounter` < 3
- `chrome://dino/` not already bookmarked

Increments `kDinoBookmarkPromptMaxTimesShownCounter` in the
`show_promo_result_callback` when the promo is actually shown.

[Test Batching] Support night mode in AutoResetCtaTransitTestRule

Night mode tests using AutoResetCtaTransitTestRule currently either
flip the theme on a live Activity (recreating it mid-batch) or use
@RequiresRestart. Add setNightModeEnabled() (backed by a reusable
ChromeNightModeState helper) so the rule reuses the Activity within
each NightModeParams group and relaunches fresh only when night mode
changes. After the test class, it finishes the themed Activity and
clears the preference so later classes in the batch start clean.

c139d6517928cfb2a36d86d30e48dac1094b6b17 [ diff ] 
[Enterprise][Proxy] Subtract implicit loopback rules from PvD matchers

`net::ProxyHostMatchingRules::Matches()` falls back to
`MatchesImplicitRules()` (`localhost`, `127.0.0.1/8`, `[::1]`,
`169.254.0.0/16`, `[fe80::]/10`, `0.0.0.0`, and `[::]`) because it is
shared with proxy bypass lists. Unlike `ProxyOverrideRules`,
`ParseRoutingRule()` did not subtract implicit rules, causing any
active Provisioning Domain (PvD) routing rule to match local
destinations and steer them to remote proxies.

Fix by:
- Calling `destination_matchers.AddRulesToSubtractImplicit()` in
  `ParseRoutingRule()`.
- Exposing `net::ProxyHostMatchingRules::kSubtractImplicitBypasses` to
  strip the internal `<-loopback>` token during persistent pref cache
  serialization and iOS `Network.framework` route translation.
- Rejecting non-list `domains`/`subnets` values, `<...>` special matcher
  tokens (`<-loopback>`, `<local>`), and `,`/`;` list delimiters in PvD
  `domains` and `subnets` without widening stripped matcher lists to `*`.

actor: Failing tool calls no longer end an Act sequence

In a composite tool that uses a nested dispatcher, we want to support
cases where an individual tool failure doesn't necessarily fail the
composite tool. For example, a search tool might attempt to search for a
given URL with a TemplateURL but watch for a failure (because the URL
doesn't have a registered TemplateURL) and fall back to using the
default search engine. Other tools may wish to do some cleanup, for
example, OpenURL could close an opened tab if the navigation for the
opened tab failed.

All of the code flow already supports this, only the state transitions
and CHECKs assumed we can never return to kStartAction. This CL adds a
test for this case and lifts the state transition restrictions.

[Autofill] Avoid retries in negative Autofill popup tests

DontAutofillForOutsideClick asserts that clicking a disabled button does
not open the Autofill popup, so leaving max_show_tries at the default of
5 spent ~19s waiting across 5 popup timeouts. In
ShowAutofillSuggestions, retries only help deflake positive assertions;
when failure is expected, each extra attempt adds another ~4.2s (a
timeout wait, throttle delay, and another click timeout).

Set max_show_tries to 1 in both DontAutofillForOutsideClick and
DontAutofillShowPopupWhenNoEnoughHeightInContentArea (which previously
used 2).

Round Event.ScrollJank.DelayedFramesPercentage4.* up

This CL adds a new feature, ScrollJankV4MetricRoundPercentageUp (enabled
by default), which modifies the logic for calculating the scroll jank v4
UMA histograms from floor(100 * delayed_frames / presented_frames) to
ceil(100 * delayed_frames / presented_frames).

This guarantees that a scroll will end up in the 0th bucket of each
scroll jank v4 UMA histogram if and only if the scroll doesn't contain
any delayed frames.

Note: This change to applies all PerScroll and FixedWindow scroll jank
v4 UMA histograms.

[iOS][Passkeys] Fix ContentAreaEvent logging bugs and split modal vs conditional

Fixes three WebAuthentication.IOS.ContentAreaEvent metrics issues and
separates modal vs conditional requests into patterned histogram
variants:

1. Prevent double-counting CreateRequested and GetRequested when
   deferring back to WebKit passthrough by passing logStartEvent=false
   on fallback.
2. Emit CreateResolvedGpm and GetResolvedGpm from PasskeyTabHelper when
   in-browser GPM passkey creation or assertion resolves.
3. Separate internal cleanup ('cleanupRequest') from AbortSignal
   cancellation ('cancelRequest') so concurrent WebKit passthrough wins
   do not log false CancelRequested samples.
4. Split WebAuthentication.IOS.ContentAreaEvent into .Modal and
   .Conditional variants alongside the unsuffixed aggregate histogram.

Test HTML form popup dismissal and blocking across panes

Add an Aura interactive UI invariant test verifying that in Split View:
1. Moving focus to the sibling pane activates it and dismisses any open
   HTML form popup in the unfocused pane.
2. Attempting to open a new HTML form popup in the unfocused pane is
   rejected.

Autofill relies on this behavior so that it only needs to check the
active WebContents tree for open HTML form popups.

fake_dmserver: Keep the macOS DM token in the user data dir

This change only has an effect when allow_fake_dmserver=true and
--use-fake-dmserver is passed.

On macOS, all browsers of the OS user share one DM token directory. A
test browser that uses fake_dmserver can overwrite the DM token of an
installed browser.

With --use-fake-dmserver, the DM token is now in Policy/Enrollment/ in
the UDD, as on Linux.

097d347cf52f9adeb96569b18d570d9ae9a324b1 [ diff ] 
[Public Transit] Allow States and Facilities to have other parents

Building on the parent/child relation that Facilities have with their
host Station, State#setParent() and Facility#setParent() are now public
and allow:

- A State to have any ConditionalState as parent. It uses the parent's
  Activity if it declares none.
- A Facility to have another, already active, Facility of the same
  host Station as parent. Facilities without a parent set still get
  their host Station as parent when entered.

The parent is set before entering the child, so TripBuilder only fills
in the default.

Exiting a parent also exits its ACTIVE children, recursively, in the
same Transition, so a child is never left ACTIVE after the state it
belongs to is gone. This is needed for States that ground a part of
another state, like the upcoming OptionalElement, which checks lazily
whether an optional Element is present: the check enters a new State
rather than mutating the owner, and that State must not outlive it.

Also add a hook for a child to skip waiting for its EXIT Conditions,
for children that stand for an Element of their parent whose id
differs from the ids of the Elements they declare.

Reland "fake_dmserver: add macOS support"

The original change broke mac-arm64-rel, because fake_dmserver
depended on Cast Core gRPC. Desktop builds no longer have that
dependency.

Differences from the original change:
- fake_dmserver builds on macOS only when the target CPU is the host
  CPU, because it runs the host protoc binary.
- The build condition is in one GN variable.
- generated_testonly also builds on macOS.
- main() makes a FileDescriptorWatcher. Without it, the policy file
  watcher crashes at startup on macOS.

Original change's description:
> fake_dmserver: add macOS support
>
> Just need to tweak some BUILD files. Windows requires more work, so I'm
> not doing it just yet.

fake_dmserver: Make the gRPC server ChromeOS-only

The gRPC server depends on Cast Core, which does not support macOS.
That dependency caused the revert of the macOS port
(crrev.com/c/7524305). Desktop does not need the gRPC server, because
the REST admin API sends remote commands there.

- On desktop, --grpc-unix-socket-uri is now an error.
- Desktop now depends on the policy protos directly. Cast Core
  supplied them before.

fake_dmserver: Move the gRPC server to its own class

The gRPC code depends on Cast Core, which does not support macOS. In
its own class, it can become ChromeOS-only without creating an #ifdef
soup in FakeDMServer.

- The function bodies do not change. The added lines are the new
  class, its header, and its includes.
- Pending wait operations and handler tasks are now deleted with the
  gRPC server at shutdown.
- EraseWaitOperation() had no caller, so it is deleted.

[🌷] Deflake ContentVerifierTest navigation on Android

Navigate in the active tab instead of opening a new tab in
ContentVerifierTest::NavigateToResourceAndExpectExtensionDisabled.

When content verification detects corruption and disables the
extension, ExtensionBrowserWindowHelper::CleanUpTabsOnUnload closes any
non-last tab committed to an extension URL. On Android, opening a new
tab via NavigateToURLInNewTab calls
android_ui_test_utils::OpenUrlInNewTab, which asserts that the tab
count increased by 1 after navigation completes, racing with tab closure
and flaking ContentVerifierTest#TamperLargeSizedResource and
ContentVerifierTest#VerificationFailureOnNavigate. Navigating in the
single active tab avoids creating a second tab that gets closed on
unload.

Verified with UTR (android_browsertests,
ContentVerifierTest.TamperLargeSizedResource):
- android-desktop-x64-rel: 21/21 passed
  (https://chromium-swarm.appspot.com/task?id=7c361e08ada5d210)
- android-desktop-x64-rel-17-tests: 21/21 passed
  (https://chromium-swarm.appspot.com/task?id=7c362759a3e3b510)

[Toolbar] Apply incognito theme color on address bar position changes

With the bottom bar enabled, incognito uses a lighter surface color at
the bottom than at the top. Moving the address bar updates
`ToolbarThemeColorProvider`, but `ToolbarPhone` ignored primary color
updates in incognito. Each layout pass used to repaint the primary color
in `onMeasure`, which hid the problem. `BottomControlsJankImprovement`
skips that repaint when the layout is unchanged, so the address bar
keeps its old color until a tab switcher transition repaints it.

We now apply primary color updates right away in incognito. Controls
position changes also switch colors without animation, like incognito
did in M156. The old 250ms fade ran while the toolbar was hidden during
the slide animation. After omnibox unfocus it showed the top color at
the bottom of the screen.

Without the bottom bar, `ToolbarThemeColorProvider` never switches
providers or runs that fade. Page theme color changes still animate.

Always store returned sync tokens

ClientResourceProvider was dropping the release sync tokens for anything
except the last release before the resource release callback runs. This
generally works but if an earlier release has a sync token from a
different sequence or the last release has no sync token there is a
synchronization problem.

Always store the sync tokens. For legacy path there is only ever a
single sync token, so this only helps if the last release has no sync
token. For the automatic path ClientSharedImage will always store the
latest sync token from each sequence so it works for all cases.

[cc] Avoid decode_failure on concurrent GPU image upload

When kUnlockDuringGpuImageOperations is enabled,
UploadImageIfNecessary() releases lock_ during the transfer cache
upload. If another thread successfully uploads the image while lock_ is
released and a failing upload then reacquires lock_, setting
decode_failure = true overwrites the entry's state even though uploaded
data is present. Guard decode_failure = true with !HasUploadedData() so
a concurrent successful upload is preserved.

[iOS] Add a doc on writing robust EarlGrey tests

EG test suppressions grew sharply in Sep-Oct 2026. Most deflake CLs
since August fixed the test rather than the product, and a few
test-side patterns came up repeatedly. This collects the ones backed by
landed deflake CLs in a short doc that coding agents, deflake agents and
reviewers can refer to.

- Adds ios/testing/docs/eg_test_best_practices.md.
- Links it from ios/best_practices.md and docs/ios/testing.md.
- The EG test creation and deflaking agent skills in ios_internal will
  point to this doc in a follow-up CL.

mojo: channel_linux: Offer eventfd upgrade between non-broker nodes

Add kMojoUseEventFdBetweenNonBrokers (disabled by default). When it is
enabled, both non-broker nodes call OfferChannelUpgrade() on activation.

It was an overlook to only upgrade to eventfd channels between broker
and non-broker. IIRC I made it this way for easier debugging and forgot
to extend. In other words, I think this transition is going to be safe.

Why it works for two non-brokers:

* Each offer only covers the outgoing direction of the side that makes
  it. It flips `ChannelLinux::offered_` when sending an upgrade offer.

* Because of this, simultaneous offers and the reciprocal offer made
  from OnControlMessage(UPGRADE_OFFER) on the IO thread can race without
  losing or duplicating an offer.

Additional consistency catch from an agent:

When handling UPGRADE_OFFER, install the read notifier only after the
shared read buffer is validated, so that SharedMemReadReady() never
observes one without the other.
